Point-in-time inventory and container views, and a batch of fixes for events that were recorded wrongly, not at all, or shown misleadingly.

- New /sg snapshot: reconstruct a player inventory or a container as it stood at a past instant, browse it in a GUI, and take items back out of it. Every take is logged and attributed, so pulling an item out of a reconstructed inventory is itself searchable history. Container snapshots need no setup and store nothing, because they are rebuilt from the deposit/withdraw log you already keep. Capturing player inventories is opt-in and off until you set snapshot.players.enabled, since it is the one capture that runs on a timer rather than reacting to events and so costs disk whether or not anyone looks; running the command while it is off tells you which key to turn on.
- FastAsyncWorldEdit edits are logged correctly again on FAWE 2.15.2. On that version Spyglass took its notes after FAWE had already written the chunk, so it read the new blocks as the "before" state and logged every placed block as a break of the material that had just been placed. Generation commands and brushes (//cyl, //pyramid, //sphere) lost their place records entirely, and //paste and //move gained phantom breaks at the destination. Logging now happens in the stage where the before and after data are both valid. FAWE 2.15.0 and earlier were never affected. Records already written by an affected build cannot be repaired, because the "placed" facts were never stored.
- Hopper, dropper and dispenser movement is recorded per slot, each record carrying that slot's exact contents before and after. A container snapshot now replays automated traffic exactly, instead of returning a confident wrong answer for a container a hopper had drained. These records are still never touched by rollback or restore. Every movement is now recorded rather than one per flow window, so servers running heavy hopper farms should watch disk and reach for the per-event toggles or a shorter per-event retention.
- Container access on animals and chest boats is logged. Horse saddle and armor slots, donkey, mule and llama chests, and chest boats produced no records at all: no deposits, no withdrawals, and no open or close pair. Minecart inventories now also emit open and close records, which the old code dropped.
- Snapshotting a double chest, or a container that has since been destroyed, opens the view instead of failing silently. The window was built one row taller than Minecraft permits, so the player got no window and no error whatsoever. Any other failure to build the view now falls back to the text listing rather than swallowing the result.
- Chiseled bookshelves, decorated pots and lecterns can be snapshotted. They hold inventories but are not containers as far as the server API is concerned, so looking at one was refused, and naming it by coordinate reported it as destroyed while it stood there full.
- Container reconstruction is more honest about what it cannot know. A change recorded in the same second you asked about is no longer dropped, an instant older than the container's whole recorded history is reported as inferred rather than certain, and a window large enough to hit the internal query cap says so instead of quietly leaving the oldest changes out. Naming a coordinate that never held a container answers plainly, and no longer generates world chunks as a side effect of the lookup.
- /sg version shows the support Discord.

Config upgrades from v2 to v3 on first boot and your existing file is backed up beside it. The two hopper transfer events changed names, and the migration carries any toggle or retention you had set on the old names across to the new ones. Stored data is unchanged and no data migration runs, so upgrading is a jar swap.
